q: Gronwall's inequality: if u(t) ≤ α(t) + ∫₀ᵗ β(s)u(s)ds with β ≥ 0, then:
opts: u(t) ≤ max α + t · max β
exp: Gronwall's inequality: u(t) ≤ α(t)exp(∫₀ᵗ β(s)ds). This is the fundamental comparison principle for differential inequalities. It is used ubiquitously to prove uniqueness and continuous dependence on parameters for ODEs, and to bound solutions of perturbed systems.
